newsitem.title: USA: Dow seen lifted by oil, interest rate mood calms.
newsitem.headline: Dow seen lifted by oil, interest rate mood calms.

text.p: U.S. stocks could open modestly higher on Monday, boosted by energy shares and a follow-through on Friday's rally.
The calming of swirling interest rate fears into a consensus is also expected to help boost the market.

"We could have a decent follow-through on Friday's gains, but nothing's set in stone," said Larry Wachtel at Prudential Securities. "The Street is becoming convinced the Fed's going to tighten rates and an increase of 25 points is built in."

"(Federal Reserve Governor Laurence) Meyer's comments in Boston over the weekend solidified the view that the Fed will pull the trigger," he said. "If we do well today, we'll probably give some back again in the next two days," he noted.
Meyer told a conference that the Fed must be vigilant about fighting inflation after August U.S. employment data,

"Some strength in the energy patch may surface and that contributes to the Dow," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock and Co. He noted that there is "a jittery sense" about energy prices, which could raise inflation concerns.
The Fed issues consumer credit data for July at 1500 EDT/1900 GMT.
The dollar was off slightly with the downside holding in Tokyo trading, stuck near 109.1 yen. In Europe, the greenback was caught in a narrow range.
General Motors shares slipped in Eurotrading, off 3/8 to 47-3/8, after the New York Times said on Sunday that several analysts cut earnings estimates for the automaker.
October IPE Brent crude futures edged up five cents to $22.59 a barrel in early trading on gas oil prices and the situation in the Middle East.
